name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q05 - Nephron unit structure and ureotelic excretion

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the structural organisation in frogs:
Statement I: Each kidney in a frog is composed of numerous structural and functional units called uriniferous tubules or nephrons.
Statement II: A thin-walled urinary bladder is situated dorsal to the rectum and empties directly into the lumen of the stomach.
Statement III: The frog eliminates its nitrogenous wastes primarily in the form of urea and is categorized as a ureotelic animal.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

मेंढक के संरचनात्मक संगठन के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: मेंढक में प्रत्येक वृक्क कई संरचनात्मक और क्रियात्मक इकाइयों से बना होता है जिन्हें मूत्रजन नलिकाएं या नेफ्रॉन कहते हैं।
कथन II: एक पतली भित्ति वाला मूत्राशय मलाशय के पृष्ठ भाग में स्थित होता है और सीधे आमाशय की गुहा में खुलता है।
कथन III: मेंढक अपने नाइट्रोजनी अपशिष्टों को मुख्य रूप से यूरिया के रूप में उत्सर्जित करता है और इसे यूरियोटेलिक प्राणी के रूप में वर्गीकृत किया जाता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Renal Functional Units
The compact bean-shaped kidneys of frogs are densely packed with thousands of coiled uriniferous tubules (nephrons) responsible for filtering blood and forming urine. This statement is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Urinary Bladder Position and Connection
The urinary bladder in frogs is located ventral (not dorsal) to the rectum and opens directly into the cloaca (not the stomach). Stating it lies dorsal to the rectum and opens into the stomach is factually false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Nitrogenous Waste Elimination
Adult frogs convert toxic ammonia into urea in the liver, which is subsequently excreted by the kidneys; hence, frogs are ureotelic organisms. This statement is factually accurate.

Final Answer
The statements identifying uriniferous tubules as renal units and designating frogs as ureotelic animals are correct, whereas the statement misplacing the urinary bladder is incorrect.

चरण 1: वृक्क की क्रियात्मक इकाइयों का मूल्यांकन
मेंढक के वृक्क कई संरचनात्मक व क्रियात्मक इकाइयों से बने होते हैं जिन्हें मूत्रजन नलिकाएं (नेफ्रॉन) कहा जाता है, जो रक्त को छानकर मूत्र निर्माण करती हैं। अतः यह कथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: मूत्राशय की स्थिति और निकास का मूल्यांकन
मेंढक का मूत्राशय मलाशय के अधर (ventral) भाग में स्थित होता है तथा अवस्कर (cloaca) में खुलता है, न कि पृष्ठ भाग में या आमाशय में। अतः यह कथन असत्य है।

चरण 3: उत्सर्जी पदार्थ का मूल्यांकन
वयस्क मेंढक मुख्य रूप से यूरिया का उत्सर्जन करता है, अतः यह एक यूरियोटेलिक प्राणी है। अतः यह कथन सत्य है।

अंतिम उत्तर
नेफ्रॉन की संरचना तथा यूरियोटेलिक स्वभाव संबंधी कथन सही हैं, जबकि मूत्राशय की स्थिति संबंधी कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement III only
Statement I and Statement II only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q06 - Frog brain divisions and cranial nerve anatomy

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the structural organisation in frogs:
Statement I: The forebrain of a frog includes olfactory lobes, paired cerebral hemispheres, and an unpaired diencephalon.
Statement II: The midbrain of a frog is characterized by a prominent pair of optic lobes.
Statement III: The medulla oblongata passes out through the foramen magnum and continues into the spinal cord enclosed in the vertebral column.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

मेंढक के संरचनात्मक संगठन के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: मेंढक के अग्र-मस्तिष्क में घ्राण पालियां, युग्मित प्रमस्तिष्क गोलार्ध और एक अयुग्मित डाइएन्सेफेलॉन सम्मिलित होते हैं।
कथन II: मेंढक का मध्य-मस्तिष्क एक प्रमुख जोड़ी दृष्टि पालियों (ऑप्टिक लोब्स) द्वारा अभिलक्षित होता है।
कथन III: मेडुला ऑबलोंगेटा महारंध्र (फोरामेन मैग्नम) से होकर बाहर निकलता है और कशेरुक दंड में बंद मेरुरज्जु के रूप में जारी रहता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Forebrain Anatomy
The anterior brain division (forebrain) consists of anterior olfactory lobes dedicated to chemosensory olfaction, paired bilateral cerebral hemispheres, and a posterior unpaired diencephalon. This statement is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Midbrain Morphology
The midbrain consists of a pair of large, dorsolateral spherical structures termed optic lobes that process visual stimuli. This statement is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Hindbrain Continuity
The hindbrain comprises the cerebellum and medulla oblongata; the latter exits the posterior brain box (cranium) via the foramen magnum to form the spinal cord within the vertebral canal. This statement is factually accurate.

Final Answer
All three statements are correct regarding the divisions, constituent parts, and spinal continuity of the frog's central nervous system.

चरण 1: अग्र-मस्तिष्क की संरचना का मूल्यांकन
अग्र-मस्तिष्क में घ्राण पालियां (ऑलफैक्ट्री लोब्स), युग्मित प्रमस्तिष्क गोलार्ध (सेरेब्रल हेमिस्फियर्स) तथा अयुग्मित डाइएन्सेफेलॉन शामिल होते हैं। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 2: मध्य-मस्तिष्क के लक्षणों का मूल्यांकन
मध्य-मस्तिष्क में एक जोड़ी बड़ी दृष्टि पालियां (ऑप्टिक लोब्स) पाई जाती हैं जो दृष्टि संवेदों का संचालन करती हैं। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 3: पश्च-मस्तिष्क और मेरुरज्जु के सातत्य का मूल्यांकन
मेडुला ऑबलोंगेटा क्रेनियम के महारंध्र (फोरामेन मैग्नम) से बाहर निकलकर कशेरुक दंड में स्थित मेरुरज्जु में परिवर्तित होता है। अतः यह विवरण भी सत्य है।

अंतिम उत्तर
अग्र-मस्तिष्क के घटकों, मध्य-मस्तिष्क की दृष्टि पालियों तथा पश्च-मस्तिष्क के मेरुरज्जु में विस्तार से संबंधित तीनों कथन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q07 - Urogenital duct paths in male and female frogs

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the structural organisation in frogs:
Statement I: In male frogs, 10 to 12 vasa efferentia emerge from the testes, enter the kidneys on their side, and open into Bidder's canal.
Statement II: In male frogs, the ureters act as urinogenital ducts that carry both urine from the kidneys and sperms from Bidder's canal to the cloaca.
Statement III: In female frogs, the oviducts and ureters join to form a common duct before discharging their contents into the urinary bladder.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

मेंढक के संरचनात्मक संगठन के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: नर मेंढक में, 10 से 12 शुक्रवाहिकाएं वृषण से निकलकर अपनी तरफ के वृक्क में प्रवेश करती हैं और बिडर नाल में खुलती हैं।
कथन II: नर मेंढक में, मूत्रवाहिनियां मूत्रजनन वाहिनियों के रूप में कार्य करती हैं जो वृक्क से मूत्र तथा बिडर नाल से शुक्राणु दोनों को अवस्कर तक ले जाती हैं।
कथन III: मादा मेंढक में, अंडवाहिनियां और मूत्रवाहिनियां मिलकर एक संयुक्त वाहिनी बनाती हैं और अपने पदार्थों को मूत्राशय में छोड़ती हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Vasa Efferentia Connection
In male frogs, 10-12 delicate ducts (vasa efferentia) leave the anterior testicular lobules, cross the mesorchium, enter the renal tissue, and connect with Bidder's canal running along the medial edge of each kidney. This statement is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Male Urinogenital Ducts
Bidder's canal drains via transverse collecting ducts into the ureter; hence, each male ureter conducts both urinary filtrate and male gametes to the cloaca, functioning as a true urinogenital duct. This statement is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Female Urogenital Openings
In female frogs, the ureters carry strictly urine from the kidneys to the cloaca, while the oviducts carry ova from the body cavity to the cloaca. The ureters and oviducts remain completely independent and open separately into the cloaca; neither enters the urinary bladder. Claiming they fuse and enter the urinary bladder is factually false.

Final Answer
The statements detailing vasa efferentia routing into Bidder's canal and the male ureters functioning as urinogenital ducts are correct, while the statement describing female duct fusion is incorrect.

चरण 1: शुक्रवाहिकाओं के मार्ग का मूल्यांकन
नर मेंढक में वृषण से 10-12 शुक्रवाहिकाएं निकलकर वृक्क में प्रवेश करती हैं तथा बिडर नाल में खुलती हैं। अतः यह कथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: नर मूत्रजनन वाहिनी का मूल्यांकन
बिडर नाल से शुक्राणु संग्रह नलिकाओं द्वारा मूत्रवाहिनी में पहुंचते हैं, अतः नर मेंढक में मूत्रवाहिनी मूत्र और शुक्राणु दोनों का वहन करती है तथा मूत्रजनन वाहिनी कहलाती है। अतः यह कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: मादा वाहिनी व्यवस्था का मूल्यांकन
मादा मेंढक में मूत्रवाहिनियां और अंडवाहिनियां पूरी तरह स्वतंत्र होती हैं तथा अवस्कर में अलग-अलग खुलती हैं; वे न तो आपस में जुड़ती हैं और न ही मूत्राशय में खुलती हैं। अतः यह कथन असत्य है।

अंतिम उत्तर
शुक्रवाहिकाओं के बिडर नाल में प्रवेश तथा नर मूत्रजनन वाहिनी संबंधी कथन सही हैं, जबकि मादा वाहिनियों के संयुक्त होने संबंधी कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Statement II and Statement III only
Statement I and Statement III only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q01 - Integumentary features and ocular protection

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the structural organisation in frogs:
Statement I: The skin of a frog is smooth, slippery, and constantly maintained in a moist condition due to the secretion of mucus.
Statement II: The colour of the dorsal side of the body is generally olive green with dark irregular spots, while the ventral side is uniformly pale yellow.
Statement III: Adult frogs never drink water orally but absorb required moisture directly through the skin.
Statement IV: The eyes of a frog are covered by an immovable opaque eyelid that prevents water entry while swimming.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

मेंढक के संरचनात्मक संगठन के संबंध में निम्नलिखित चार कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: मेंढक की त्वचा श्लेष्मा (म्यूकस) के स्राव के कारण चिकनी, फिसलनदार तथा निरंतर नम बनी रहती है।
कथन II: शरीर की पृष्ठ सतह का रंग सामान्यतः गहरे अनियमित धब्बों के साथ जैतून जैसा हरा (ऑलिव ग्रीन) होता है, जबकि अधर सतह एकसमान हल्की पीली होती है।
कथन III: वयस्क मेंढक कभी भी मुख द्वारा पानी नहीं पीते हैं बल्कि आवश्यक नमी को सीधे त्वचा द्वारा अवशोषित करते हैं।
कथन IV: मेंढक के नेत्र एक अचल अपारदर्शी पलक से ढके रहते हैं जो तैरते समय पानी के प्रवेश को रोकती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Skin Moisture and Mucus
Frogs possess numerous cutaneous mucous glands that continuously release mucus, ensuring the epidermal surface remains smooth, slippery, and moist for cutaneous respiration. Thus, the first statement is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Body Coloration Pattern
The textbook explicitly describes the dorsal body coloration as olive green bearing dark irregular spots and the ventral skin as uniformly pale yellow, which serves as camouflage. Thus, the second statement is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Hydration Mechanism
Frogs never ingest water by drinking; rather, their permeable, vascular integument facilitates direct osmotic absorption of moisture from damp soil and aquatic environments. Thus, the third statement is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of Ocular Covering
The bulging eyes of a frog are protected in water by a transparent, movable nictitating membrane rather than an immovable opaque eyelid. Thus, the fourth statement is factually false.

Final Answer
The statements regarding moist mucous skin, olive-green/yellow coloration, and dermal water absorption are correct, whereas the statement describing an immovable opaque eyelid is incorrect.

चरण 1: त्वचा की नमी और श्लेष्मा का मूल्यांकन
मेंढक में त्वचीय श्लेष्मा ग्रंथियां लगातार म्यूकस का स्राव करती हैं जिससे त्वचा चिकनी, नम और फिसलनदार बनी रहती है, जो त्वचीय श्वसन में सहायक है। अतः पहला कथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: शरीर के रंगांकन का मूल्यांकन
पाठ्यपुस्तक के अनुसार मेंढक की पृष्ठ सतह गहरे अनियमित धब्बों के साथ जैतून जैसी हरी और अधर सतह एकसमान हल्की पीली होती है। अतः दूसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: जलयोजन क्रियाविधि का मूल्यांकन
मेंढक मुख से पानी कभी नहीं पीते, बल्कि अपनी पारगम्य त्वचा द्वारा सीधे जल अवशोषित करते हैं। अतः तीसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 4: नेत्र आवरण का मूल्यांकन
मेंढक के नेत्र एक पारदर्शी गतिशील निमेषक पटल (निक्टिटेटिंग मेम्ब्रेन) से ढके रहते हैं, न कि अचल अपारदर्शी पलक से। अतः चौथा कथन असत्य है।

अंतिम उत्तर
श्लेष्मायुक्त नम त्वचा, पृष्ठीय/अधरीय रंगांकन तथा त्वचीय जल अवशोषण संबंधी कथन सही हैं, जबकि अचल अपारदर्शी पलक संबंधी कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I, II, and III only
Statements II, III, and IV only
Statements I, III, and IV only
Statements I, II, III, and IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q02 - Alimentary canal length and digestive tract pathway

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the structural organisation in frogs:
Statement I: The alimentary canal of a frog is relatively short because frogs are carnivores, which naturally reduces the required length of the intestine.
Statement II: In the stomach, food is partially digested by the action of hydrochloric acid and gastric juices, converting it into chyme.
Statement III: The duodenum receives bile from the gall bladder and pancreatic juice from the pancreas via a common bile duct.
Statement IV: Undigested solid waste passes directly from the rectum into the urinary bladder before being discharged from the body.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

मेंढक के संरचनात्मक संगठन के संबंध में निम्नलिखित चार कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: मेंढक की आहार नाल अपेक्षाकृत छोटी होती है क्योंकि मेंढक मांसाहारी होते हैं, जिससे आंत की आवश्यक लंबाई कम हो जाती है।
कथन II: आमाशय में हाइड्रोक्लोरिक अम्ल और जठर रस की क्रिया द्वारा भोजन का आंशिक पाचन होता है, जो इसे कायम में बदल देता है।
कथन III: ग्रहणी (डुओडेनम), एक सामान्य पित्त वाहिनी के माध्यम से पित्ताशय से पित्त रस तथा अग्न्याशय से अग्न्याशयी रस प्राप्त करती है।
कथन IV: अपचित ठोस अपशिष्ट शरीर से बाहर निकलने से पहले मलाशय से सीधे मूत्राशय में जाता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Alimentary Canal Length
Because adult frogs consume animal prey that is easily broken down, the intestine is relatively short, making the entire digestive canal compact. Thus, the first statement is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Gastric Digestion
The gastric mucosa secretes hydrochloric acid (HCl) and proteolytic gastric juices that chemically churn and digest food into acidic semi-fluid pulp called chyme. Thus, the second statement is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Duodenal Secretions
The duodenum is the first portion of the small intestine and receives both alkaline bile from the gall bladder and digestive enzymes from the pancreas through a shared common bile duct. Thus, the third statement is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of Solid Waste Route
Undigested solid faecal waste moves from the intestine into the rectum and is expelled directly to the exterior through the cloaca. It never enters the urinary bladder, which is reserved exclusively for storing urine. Thus, the fourth statement is factually false.

Final Answer
The statements detailing the short carnivorous intestine, gastric production of chyme, and common bile duct reception are correct, whereas the statement directing solid waste into the urinary bladder is incorrect.

चरण 1: आहार नाल की लंबाई का मूल्यांकन
मेंढक मांसाहारी होते हैं जिससे इनकी आंत की लंबाई छोटी होती है और पूरी आहार नाल संक्षिप्त रहती है। अतः पहला कथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: आमाशयी पाचन का मूल्यांकन
आमाशय की भित्ति से स्रावित हाइड्रोक्लोरिक अम्ल तथा जठर रस भोजन को आंशिक रूप से पचाकर कायम (chyme) बनाते हैं। अतः दूसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: ग्रहणी के स्राव का मूल्यांकन
ग्रहणी एक उभयनिष्ठ सामान्य पित्त वाहिनी के माध्यम से पित्ताशय से पित्त रस तथा अग्न्याशय से अग्न्याशयी रस प्राप्त करती है। अतः तीसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 4: अपचित अपशिष्ट के मार्ग का मूल्यांकन
अपचित ठोस मल मलाशय से होकर सीधे अवस्कर द्वारा बाहर निकलता है; यह कभी भी मूत्राशय में नहीं जाता। मूत्राशय केवल मूत्र संग्रह के लिए होता है। अतः चौथा कथन असत्य है।

अंतिम उत्तर
संक्षिप्त मांसाहारी आहार नाल, आमाशय में कायम निर्माण तथा सामान्य पित्त वाहिनी संबंधी कथन सही हैं, जबकि मल के मूत्राशय में जाने संबंधी कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I and IV only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q03 - Heart anatomy accessory chambers and portal circuits

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the structural organisation in frogs:
Statement I: The heart of a frog is a muscular organ having three chambers—two atria and one ventricle—enclosed by a pericardium.
Statement II: A triangular chamber called sinus venosus joins the right atrium and receives deoxygenated blood through the major vena cava.
Statement III: The single ventricle opens into a sac-like conus arteriosus located on the ventral surface of the heart.
Statement IV: The specialized vascular connection between the liver and intestine in frogs is termed the renal portal system.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

मेंढक के संरचनात्मक संगठन के संबंध में निम्नलिखित चार कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: मेंढक का हृदय एक पेशीय अंग है जिसमें तीन कोष्ठक—दो अलिंद और एक निलय—होते हैं, जो पेरिकार्डियम से ढका रहता है।
कथन II: शिरा कोटर (साइनस वेनोसस) नामक एक त्रिकोणीय कोष्ठ दाएं अलिंद से जुड़ता है और महाशिराओं से विऑक्सीजनित रक्त प्राप्त करता है।
कथन III: एकल निलय हृदय के अधर (वेंट्रल) तल पर स्थित एक थैली जैसी रचना कोनस आर्टेरियोसस में खुलता है।
कथन IV: मेंढक में यकृत तथा आंत के बीच पाए जाने वाले विशिष्ट संवहनी संबंध को वृक्क निवाहिका तंत्र (रीनल पोर्टल सिस्टम) कहा जाता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Heart Chamber Architecture
The frog's heart possesses two receiving atria and a single muscular ventricle enveloped by the pericardial membrane. Thus, the first statement is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Sinus Venosus Connection
Systemic venous blood returns through anterior and posterior vena cava into the triangular sinus venosus, which opens dorsally into the right atrium. Thus, the second statement is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Conus Arteriosus Position
Blood pumped by ventricular systole exits into the sac-like conus arteriosus arising from the ventral surface of the heart before branching into aortic arches. Thus, the third statement is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of Portal Circuit Terminology
The venous connection between the digestive tract (intestine) and liver is designated as the hepatic portal system, whereas the renal portal system connects the lower body regions with the kidneys. The fourth statement swaps these terms and is therefore factually false.

Final Answer
The statements describing the three-chambered pericardial heart, sinus venosus reception into the right atrium, and ventral conus arteriosus are correct, whereas the statement misnaming the hepatic portal connection is incorrect.

चरण 1: हृदय के कोष्ठकों की संरचना का मूल्यांकन
मेंढक का हृदय दो अलिंद और एक निलय युक्त तीन कोष्ठकीय संरचना है जो हृदयावरण (पेरिकार्डियम) से आच्छादित होती है। अतः पहला कथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: शिरा कोटर के संबंध का मूल्यांकन
शिरा कोटर (साइनस वेनोसस) एक त्रिकोणीय कोष्ठ है जो महाशिराओं से अशुद्ध रक्त लेकर दाएं अलिंद में खुलता है। अतः दूसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: कोनस आर्टेरियोसस की स्थिति का मूल्यांकन
एकल निलय हृदय के अधर (वेंट्रल) तल पर स्थित थैलीनुमा रचना कोनस आर्टेरियोसस में खुलता है। अतः तीसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 4: निवाहिका तंत्र की शब्दावली का मूल्यांकन
यकृत और आंत के मध्य संवहनी संबंध को यकृत निवाहिका तंत्र (हिपेटिक पोर्टल सिस्टम) कहते हैं, जबकि वृक्क निवाहिका तंत्र निचले अंगों व वृक्कों के बीच होता है। अतः चौथा कथन असत्य है।

अंतिम उत्तर
तीन कोष्ठकीय हृदय, दाएं अलिंद में शिरा कोटर का खुलना तथा अधर कोनस आर्टेरियोसस संबंधी कथन सही हैं, जबकि यकृत निवाहिका तंत्र को वृक्क निवाहिका तंत्र बताने वाला कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Statements II, III, and IV only
Statements I and IV only
Statements I, II, and III only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q04 - Urogenital connections and sexually dimorphic ducts

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the structural organisation in frogs:
Statement I: In male frogs, 10 to 12 vasa efferentia emerge from the testes, enter the kidneys, and open into Bidder's canal.
Statement II: In male frogs, the ureters act as urinogenital ducts that carry both urine from the kidneys and spermatozoa from Bidder's canal into the cloaca.
Statement III: In female frogs, the ovaries maintain a direct structural and functional connection with the kidneys through Bidder's canal.
Statement IV: In female frogs, the paired ureters and oviducts open separately into the cloaca.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

मेंढक के संरचनात्मक संगठन के संबंध में निम्नलिखित चार कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: नर मेंढक में, 10 से 12 शुक्रवाहिकाएं (वासा इफेरेंशिया) वृषण से निकलकर वृक्कों में प्रवेश करती हैं और बिडर नाल में खुलती हैं।
कथन II: नर मेंढक में, मूत्रवाहिनियां मूत्रजनन वाहिनियों के रूप में कार्य करती हैं जो वृक्क से मूत्र तथा बिडर नाल से शुक्राणु दोनों को अवस्कर तक ले जाती हैं।
कथन III: मादा मेंढक में, अंडाशय बिडर नाल के माध्यम से वृक्क के साथ सीधा संरचनात्मक और क्रियात्मक संबंध बनाए रखते हैं।
कथन IV: मादा मेंढक में, युग्मित मूत्रवाहिनियां और अंडवाहिनियां अवस्कर में अलग-अलग खुलती हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Male Vasa Efferentia Routing
10 to 12 vasa efferentia originate from each testis, cross the peritoneal mesorchium, enter the adjacent kidney, and open directly into Bidder's canal. Thus, the first statement is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Male Urinogenital Duct Function
Bidder's canal drains via longitudinal collecting tubules into the ureters; consequently, the male ureters conduct both excretory urine and male gametes to the cloaca, functioning as urinogenital ducts. Thus, the second statement is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Female Ovarian and Renal Independence
In female frogs, the ovaries lie adjacent to the kidneys but have no structural or functional relationship with them. Female kidneys completely lack Bidder's canal. Thus, claiming that ovaries communicate with the kidneys via Bidder's canal is factually false.

Step 4: Evaluation of Female Urogenital Openings
In female frogs, the ureters discharge urine into the cloaca, while the paired convoluted oviducts independently discharge ova into the cloaca. They remain completely distinct without fusing. Thus, the fourth statement is factually accurate.

Final Answer
The statements describing vasa efferentia entering Bidder's canal, male ureters acting as urinogenital ducts, and female ureters and oviducts opening separately into the cloaca are correct, while the statement linking female ovaries to Bidder's canal is incorrect.

चरण 1: नर शुक्रवाहिकाओं के मार्ग का मूल्यांकन
नर मेंढक में वृषण से 10-12 शुक्रवाहिकाएं निकलकर मेसोर्कियम द्वारा वृक्क में प्रवेश करती हैं और बिडर नाल में खुलती हैं। अतः पहला कथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: नर मूत्रजनन वाहिनी के कार्य का मूल्यांकन
बिडर नाल मूत्रवाहिनी से जुड़ती है, जिससे नर में मूत्रवाहिनियां मूत्र तथा शुक्राणु दोनों का वहन करती हैं और मूत्रजनन वाहिनी कहलाती हैं। अतः दूसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: मादा अंडाशय और वृक्क के संबंध का मूल्यांकन
मादा मेंढक में अंडाशयों का वृक्क से कोई क्रियात्मक संबंध नहीं होता और मादा में बिडर नाल अनुपस्थित होती है। अतः बिडर नाल द्वारा संबंध बताना असत्य है।

चरण 4: मादा जननमूत्र निकास का मूल्यांकन
मादा में मूत्रवाहिनियां केवल मूत्र लाती हैं और अंडवाहिनियां अंडाणु लाती हैं; दोनों अवस्कर में पूरी तरह अलग-अलग खुलती हैं। अतः चौथा कथन सत्य है।

अंतिम उत्तर
शुक्रवाहिकाओं के बिडर नाल में प्रवेश, नर मूत्रजनन वाहिनी तथा मादा वाहिनियों के अलग-अलग खुलने संबंधी कथन सही हैं, जबकि मादा अंडाशय को बिडर नाल से जोड़ने वाला कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I, II, and III only
Statements II, III, and IV only
Statements I, III, and IV only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q01 - Taxonomic status morphology and protective coloration

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding the structural organisation in frogs:
Statement I: The Indian bullfrog, Rana tigrina, belongs to class Amphibia of phylum Chordata.
Statement II: The body of an adult frog is divisible into head, neck, trunk, and tail.
Statement III: Frogs possess the ability to change their skin colour for camouflage, a protective coloration termed mimicry.
Statement IV: Adult frogs never drink water orally but absorb required moisture directly through their skin.
Statement V: The feet of the hind limbs possess webbed digits that assist in swimming.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

मेंढक के संरचनात्मक संगठन के संबंध में निम्नलिखित पांच कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: भारतीय मेंढक, राणा टिग्रीना, संघ कॉर्डेटा के वर्ग एम्फीबिया (उभयचर) से संबंधित है।
कथन II: वयस्क मेंढक का शरीर सिर, गर्दन, धड़ और पूंछ में विभाजित होता है।
कथन III: मेंढकों में छिपने के लिए त्वचा का रंग बदलने की क्षमता होती है, इस सुरक्षात्मक रंगांकन को मिमिक्री (अनुकृति) कहा जाता है।
कथन IV: वयस्क मेंढक कभी भी मुख से पानी नहीं पीते हैं बल्कि आवश्यक नमी को सीधे त्वचा द्वारा अवशोषित करते हैं।
कथन V: पश्चपादों के पंजों में पादजालयुक्त अंगुलियां होती हैं जो तैरने में सहायता करती हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Taxonomy and Species Identity
The common Indian frog is scientifically named Rana tigrina and is classified under phylum Chordata and class Amphibia. Thus, the first statement is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Body Regionalization
The body of a frog is divided solely into two regions: head and trunk. Both neck and tail are completely absent in the adult animal. Thus, the second statement is factually false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Camouflage and Mimicry
Frogs change colour to blend into grasses and dry backgrounds to hide from natural predators. This protective coloration is explicitly defined as mimicry. Thus, the third statement is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of Hydration Mechanism
Frogs never drink water through the mouth; rather, they absorb environmental water directly across their thin, moist, and vascular skin. Thus, the fourth statement is factually accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of Appendicular Adaptations
The muscular hind limbs end in five digits joined by cutaneous webbing (webbed feet) that acts like paddles for swimming. Thus, the fifth statement is factually accurate.

Final Answer
The statements identifying taxonomic placement, mimicry coloration, dermal water absorption, and webbed feet are correct, whereas the statement including a neck and tail in body division is incorrect.

चरण 1: वर्गिकी तथा जाति की पहचान का मूल्यांकन
भारतीय मेंढक का वैज्ञानिक नाम राणा टिग्रीना है और यह संघ कॉर्डेटा के वर्ग एम्फीबिया के अंतर्गत आता है। अतः पहला कथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: शरीर के प्रभाजनों का मूल्यांकन
मेंढक का शरीर केवल सिर और धड़ में विभाजित होता है; वयस्क मेंढक में गर्दन और पूंछ दोनों अनुपस्थित होते हैं। अतः दूसरा कथन असत्य है।

चरण 3: छद्मावरण तथा अनुकृति का मूल्यांकन
घास और सूखी भूमि में शत्रुओं से छिपने के लिए मेंढक रंग बदलने की क्षमता रखते हैं; इस सुरक्षात्मक रंगांकन को मिमिक्री कहते हैं। अतः तीसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 4: जल अवशोषण की विधि का मूल्यांकन
मेंढक मुख से कभी पानी नहीं पीते, बल्कि अपनी नम त्वचा के माध्यम से परिवेश से जल अवशोषित करते हैं। अतः चौथा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 5: पादों के अनुकूलन का मूल्यांकन
पश्चपाद की अंगुलियों के बीच पादजाल (वेब) उपस्थित होता है जो पानी में तैरने में चप्पू की तरह सहायता करता है। अतः पांचवां कथन सत्य है।

अंतिम उत्तर
वर्गिकी पहचान, अनुकृति रंगांकन, त्वचीय जल अवशोषण तथा पादजाल संबंधी कथन सही हैं, जबकि गर्दन व पूंछ की उपस्थिति बताने वाला कथन गलत है।

answer.text: I, III, IV, and V only
I, II, III, and IV only
II, III, IV, and V only
I, II, III, IV, and V

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q02 - Visceral digestive respiratory and circulatory adaptations

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding the structural organisation in frogs:
Statement I: The alimentary canal is short because frogs are carnivores, which naturally reduces the required length of the intestine.
Statement II: During peak summer aestivation and peak winter hibernation, gaseous exchange in frogs takes place exclusively through the lungs.
Statement III: Bile from the liver emulsifies lipids, while pancreatic enzymes digest carbohydrates and proteins in the duodenum.
Statement IV: Red blood cells (erythrocytes) of frogs are nucleated, biconvex, and contain the red pigment haemoglobin.
Statement V: A dorsal triangular chamber called sinus venosus joins the right atrium and receives systemic blood through the vena cava.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

मेंढक के संरचनात्मक संगठन के संबंध में निम्नलिखित पांच कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: आहार नाल छोटी होती है क्योंकि मेंढक मांसाहारी होते हैं, जिससे आंत की आवश्यक लंबाई घट जाती है।
कथन II: अत्यधिक ग्रीष्म निष्क्रियता और शीत निष्क्रियता के दौरान मेंढक में गैसीय विनिमय केवल फेफड़ों द्वारा होता है।
कथन III: यकृत से स्रावित पित्त रस वसा का इमल्सीकरण करता है, जबकि अग्न्याशयी रस ग्रहणी में कार्बोहाइड्रेट और प्रोटीन का पाचन करता है।
कथन IV: मेंढक के लाल रक्त कण (आरबीसी) केंद्रकयुक्त, उभयोत्तल होते हैं और इनमें लाल वर्णक हीमोग्लोबिन पाया जाता है।
कथन V: शिरा कोटर (साइनस वेनोसस) नामक एक पृष्ठ-स्थित त्रिकोणीय कोष्ठ दाएं अलिंद से जुड़ता है और महाशिराओं से दैहिक रक्त प्राप्त करता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Gut Length Adaptation
Because adult frogs feed on animal matter which requires shorter digestive processing than cellulose, the intestine is reduced in length, making the alimentary canal short. Thus, the first statement is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Respiration During Dormancy
During aestivation and hibernation, adult frogs are buried deep in mud with mouths closed; pulmonary breathing stops, and gaseous exchange occurs solely across the moist vascular skin (cutaneous respiration). Thus, claiming that dormancy respiration occurs via the lungs is factually false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Digestive Gland Functions
Liver-secreted bile emulsifies dietary fats, while pancreatic juice containing amylases and proteases digests carbohydrates and proteins within the duodenum. Thus, the third statement is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of Blood Cell Morphology
Amphibian erythrocytes are oval, nucleated cells containing haemoglobin pigment for oxygen delivery. Thus, the fourth statement is factually accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of Sinus Venosus Anatomy
The sinus venosus is a triangular accessory chamber receiving systemic deoxygenated blood through the major vena cava and emptying directly into the right atrium. Thus, the fifth statement is factually accurate.

Final Answer
The statements describing the short carnivorous gut, enzymatic actions of bile and pancreatic juice, nucleated erythrocytes, and sinus venosus anatomy are correct, while the statement asserting pulmonary respiration during dormancy is incorrect.

चरण 1: आहार नाल की लंबाई का मूल्यांकन
मांसाहारी आहार के सुगम पाचन के कारण मेंढक की आंत छोटी होती है और पूरी आहार नाल संक्षिप्त रहती है। अतः पहला कथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: सुप्तावस्था में श्वसन का मूल्यांकन
ग्रीष्म व शीत निष्क्रियता के दौरान फुप्फुसीय श्वसन पूरी तरह स्थगित रहता है और गैसीय विनिमय केवल त्वचा द्वारा होता है। अतः फेफड़ों द्वारा श्वसन का दावा असत्य है।

चरण 3: पाचक ग्रंथियों के कार्यों का मूल्यांकन
पित्त रस वसा का इमल्सीकरण करता है तथा अग्न्याशयी रस ग्रहणी में कार्बोहाइड्रेट और प्रोटीन को पचाता है। अतः तीसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 4: रक्ताणुओं की संरचना का मूल्यांकन
मेंढक के आरबीसी केंद्रकयुक्त होते हैं तथा इनमें हीमोग्लोबिन वर्णक पाया जाता है। अतः चौथा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 5: शिरा कोटर के विन्यास का मूल्यांकन
शिरा कोटर महाशिराओं से अशुद्ध रक्त प्राप्त करके दाएं अलिंद में खुलता है। अतः पांचवां कथन सत्य है।

अंतिम उत्तर
संक्षिप्त आहार नाल, पाचक रसों के कार्य, केंद्रकयुक्त आरबीसी तथा शिरा कोटर संबंधी कथन सही हैं, जबकि सुप्तावस्था में फेफड़ों द्वारा श्वसन संबंधी कथन गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q03 - Neural urogenital pathways and endocrine coordination

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding the structural organisation in frogs:
Statement I: In male frogs, 10 to 12 vasa efferentia arise from the testes, enter the kidneys, and communicate with Bidder's canal.
Statement II: In female frogs, the ovaries have no functional connection with the kidneys, and the paired oviducts open separately into the cloaca.
Statement III: There are twelve pairs of cranial nerves originating from the brain in an adult frog.
Statement IV: A thin-walled urinary bladder is situated ventral to the rectum and opens directly into the cloaca.
Statement V: In male frogs, the ureters act as urinogenital ducts that convey both urine and spermatozoa to the cloaca.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

मेंढक के संरचनात्मक संगठन के संबंध में निम्नलिखित पांच कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: नर मेंढक में, 10 से 12 शुक्रवाहिकाएं (वासा इफेरेंशिया) वृषण से निकलकर वृक्कों में प्रवेश करती हैं और बिडर नाल से जुड़ती हैं।
कथन II: मादा मेंढक में, अंडाशयों का वृक्क के साथ कोई क्रियात्मक संबंध नहीं होता और युग्मित अंडवाहिनियां अवस्कर में अलग-अलग खुलती हैं।
कथन III: एक वयस्क मेंढक के मस्तिष्क से बारह जोड़ी कपाल तंत्रिकाएं निकलती हैं।
कथन IV: एक पतली भित्ति वाला मूत्राशय मलाशय के अधर (ventral) भाग में स्थित होता है और सीधे अवस्कर में खुलता है।
कथन V: नर मेंढक में, मूत्रवाहिनियां मूत्रजनन वाहिनियों के रूप में कार्य करती हैं जो मूत्र तथा शुक्राणु दोनों को अवस्कर तक ले जाती हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Vasa Efferentia and Bidder's Canal
In male frogs, 10-12 vasa efferentia emerge from the testicular lobules, traverse the mesorchium into the kidney, and discharge into Bidder's canal. Thus, the first statement is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Female Ovarian and Renal Autonomy
Ovaries lie adjacent to kidneys but possess no functional connection with them; ova are shed into the coelom and collected by long oviducts opening independently into the cloaca. Thus, the second statement is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Cranial Nerve Enumeration
Amphibian brains give rise to exactly 10 pairs of cranial nerves, not 12 pairs (which is characteristic of amniotes like reptiles, birds, and mammals). Thus, the third statement is factually false.

Step 4: Evaluation of Urinary Bladder Position
The bilobed, thin-walled urinary bladder lies ventral to the rectum and opens directly into the ventral floor of the cloaca. Thus, the fourth statement is factually accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of Male Urinogenital Ducts
Because male frog ureters carry both urinary wastes from collecting tubules and spermatozoa from Bidder's canal, they function as urinogenital ducts. Thus, the fifth statement is factually accurate.

Final Answer
The statements detailing male vasa efferentia routing, female oviduct separation from kidneys, urinary bladder anatomy, and male urinogenital duct function are correct, while the statement enumerating twelve pairs of cranial nerves is incorrect.

चरण 1: शुक्रवाहिकाओं और बिडर नाल का मूल्यांकन
नर मेंढक में वृषण से 10-12 शुक्रवाहिकाएं निकलकर वृक्क में प्रवेश करती हैं और बिडर नाल में खुलती हैं। अतः पहला कथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: मादा जनन अंगों और वृक्क की स्वतंत्रता का मूल्यांकन
मादा मेंढक में अंडाशयों का वृक्क से कोई क्रियात्मक संबंध नहीं होता और अंडवाहिनियां अवस्कर में अलग से खुलती हैं। अतः दूसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: कपाल तंत्रिकाओं की संख्या का मूल्यांकन
मेंढक के मस्तिष्क से ठीक 10 जोड़ी कपाल तंत्रिकाएं निकलती हैं, न कि 12 जोड़ी। अतः तीसरा कथन असत्य है।

चरण 4: मूत्राशय की स्थिति का मूल्यांकन
पतली भित्ति वाला मूत्राशय मलाशय के अधर तल पर स्थित होता है और अवस्कर में खुलता है। अतः चौथा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 5: नर मूत्रजनन वाहिनी के कार्य का मूल्यांकन
नर मेंढक की मूत्रवाहिनियां मूत्र तथा शुक्राणु दोनों का वहन करती हैं, अतः इन्हें मूत्रजनन वाहिनी कहा जाता है। अतः पांचवां कथन सत्य है।

अंतिम उत्तर
शुक्रवाहिकाओं के बिडर नाल में प्रवेश, मादा वाहिनियों के स्वतंत्र निकास, मूत्राशय की स्थिति तथा नर मूत्रजनन वाहिनी संबंधी कथन सही हैं, जबकि 12 जोड़ी कपाल तंत्रिकाएं बताने वाला कथन गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q01 - Sense organs of frog and their sensory modalities

questiontext.text:
Match the sense organs of frog in List I with their corresponding sensory functions in List II:

List I List II
A. Sensory papillaeI. Smell
B. Taste budsII. Touch
C. Nasal epitheliumIII. Hearing and balancing
D. Tympanum with internal earIV. Taste

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Determine the sensory function of sensory papillae.
In frogs, sensory papillae are skin receptors that act as the organs of touch. Therefore, sensory papillae match with touch.

Step 2: Determine the sensory function of taste buds.
Taste buds are chemical receptors located within the buccal cavity that function as the organs of taste. Therefore, taste buds match with taste.

Step 3: Determine the sensory function of nasal epithelium.
The nasal epithelium lines the olfactory chambers and functions as the organ of smell. Therefore, nasal epithelium matches with smell.

Step 4: Determine the sensory function of tympanum with internal ear.
The tympanum is visible externally and works in conjunction with the internal ear to receive acoustic vibrations and maintain equilibrium, serving as the organ of hearing and balancing. Therefore, tympanum with internal ear matches with hearing and balancing.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Combining these pairs gives: Sensory papillae – Touch; Taste buds – Taste; Nasal epithelium – Smell; Tympanum with internal ear – Hearing and balancing. Thus, the correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

answer.text: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q02 - Morphological structures of frog and their functions

questiontext.text:
Match the external morphological structures of frog in List I with their descriptions or functions in List II:

List I List II
A. Nictitating membraneI. Helps in swimming in water
B. Webbed feetII. Produce sound in male frogs
C. Copulatory padIII. Protects bulged eyes while in water
D. Vocal sacsIV. Present on the first digit of male forelimbs

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the role of the nictitating membrane.
Frogs have bulged eyes covered by a transparent nictitating membrane that provides physical protection while the animal is submerged in water. Therefore, nictitating membrane matches with protecting bulged eyes while in water.

Step 2: Identify the role of webbed feet.
The hind limbs end in five digits joined by webs of skin (webbed digits), which function as paddles to aid swimming. Therefore, webbed feet match with helping in swimming in water.

Step 3: Identify the nature and position of copulatory pad.
Frogs show sexual dimorphism; male frogs possess a copulatory pad on the first digit of each forelimb, which is completely absent in females. Therefore, copulatory pad matches with being present on the first digit of male forelimbs.

Step 4: Identify the role of vocal sacs.
Male frogs possess a pair of sound-producing vocal sacs beneath the throat that amplify croaking to attract mates. Therefore, vocal sacs match with producing sound in male frogs.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Assembling the derived pairs: Nictitating membrane – Protects bulged eyes while in water; Webbed feet – Helps in swimming in water; Copulatory pad – Present on the first digit of male forelimbs; Vocal sacs – Produce sound in male frogs. Thus, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q03 - Brain regions of frog and their constituent structures

questiontext.text:
Match the regions of the central nervous system of frog in List I with their constituent structures or characteristics in List II:

List I List II
A. ForebrainI. Olfactory lobes, paired cerebral hemispheres, and unpaired diencephalon
B. MidbrainII. Passes through foramen magnum to continue into spinal cord
C. HindbrainIII. Characterised by a pair of optic lobes
D. Medulla oblongataIV. Consists of cerebellum and medulla oblongata

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the anatomical parts of the forebrain.
In frogs, the brain is enclosed within the cranium. The forebrain consists of olfactory lobes anteriorly, followed by paired cerebral hemispheres and an unpaired diencephalon. Therefore, forebrain matches with olfactory lobes, paired cerebral hemispheres, and unpaired diencephalon.

Step 2: Identify the anatomical parts of the midbrain.
The midbrain of frog is prominently characterised by a pair of dorsolateral optic lobes. Therefore, midbrain matches with being characterised by a pair of optic lobes.

Step 3: Identify the components of the hindbrain.
The hindbrain of frog is composed of two distinct regions: a small transverse cerebellum and a posterior medulla oblongata. Therefore, hindbrain matches with consisting of cerebellum and medulla oblongata.

Step 4: Trace the continuation of the medulla oblongata.
The medulla oblongata emerges out of the cranial cavity through the large posterior opening called the foramen magnum and continues posteriorly as the spinal cord inside the vertebral column. Therefore, medulla oblongata matches with passing through the foramen magnum to continue into spinal cord.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Combining these pairs: Forebrain – Olfactory lobes, paired cerebral hemispheres, and unpaired diencephalon; Midbrain – Characterised by a pair of optic lobes; Hindbrain – Consists of cerebellum and medulla oblongata; Medulla oblongata – Passes through foramen magnum to continue into spinal cord. Thus, the correct matching is A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q04 - Vascular structures of frog and their anatomical roles

questiontext.text:
Match the circulatory structures of frog in List I with their descriptions in List II:

List I List II
A. Sinus venosusI. Sac-like structure on ventral side of heart opening from ventricle
B. Conus arteriosusII. Venous connection between kidney and lower parts of body
C. Hepatic portal systemIII. Triangular structure joining right atrium and receiving venae cavae
D. Renal portal systemIV. Venous connection between liver and intestine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Characterize the sinus venosus.
The sinus venosus is a triangular chamber situated on the dorsal side of the frog heart that joins the right atrium and receives deoxygenated blood through the major veins called venae cavae. Therefore, sinus venosus matches with triangular structure joining right atrium and receiving venae cavae.

Step 2: Characterize the conus arteriosus.
The muscular ventricle pumps blood out into a funnel- or sac-like conus arteriosus located on the ventral surface of the heart, which then bifurcates into aortic trunks. Therefore, conus arteriosus matches with sac-like structure on ventral side of heart opening from ventricle.

Step 3: Characterize the hepatic portal system.
The hepatic portal system represents a specialised venous pathway that collects blood from the alimentary canal (intestine) and delivers it to the liver before returning to the heart. Therefore, hepatic portal system matches with venous connection between liver and intestine.

Step 4: Characterize the renal portal system.
The renal portal system is a specialised venous arrangement that transports venous blood from the hind limbs and lower pelvic regions directly to the kidneys. Therefore, renal portal system matches with venous connection between kidney and lower parts of body.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Synthesizing the matches: Sinus venosus – Triangular structure joining right atrium and receiving venae cavae; Conus arteriosus – Sac-like structure on ventral side of heart opening from ventricle; Hepatic portal system – Venous connection between liver and intestine; Renal portal system – Venous connection between kidney and lower parts of body. Thus, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

answer.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q05 - Digestive secretions of frog and their specific actions

questiontext.text:
Match the secretions and substances of frog in List I with their functions or roles in List II:

List I List II
A. BileI. Digestion of carbohydrates and proteins
B. Gastric juice and HClII. Keeps skin smooth, moist, and slippery
C. Pancreatic juiceIII. Emulsification of dietary fats
D. MucusIV. Breakdown of food to produce chyme in stomach

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the role of bile.
Bile is synthesized by the liver, stored in the gall bladder, and released into the duodenum via the common bile duct to emulsify large fat globules. Therefore, bile matches with emulsification of dietary fats.

Step 2: Identify the role of gastric juice and hydrochloric acid.
Gastric juice and HCl are secreted by the walls of the stomach, initiating protein breakdown and reducing ingested food into a semi-liquid mass known as chyme. Therefore, gastric juice and HCl match with breakdown of food to produce chyme in stomach.

Step 3: Identify the role of pancreatic juice.
Pancreatic juice is produced by the pancreas and delivered to the duodenum; it contains digestive enzymes responsible for digesting carbohydrates and proteins. Therefore, pancreatic juice matches with digestion of carbohydrates and proteins.

Step 4: Identify the role of mucus.
Mucus is continuously secreted by cutaneous glands in the skin, keeping it moist, smooth, and slippery to facilitate cutaneous respiration and reduce friction. Therefore, mucus matches with keeping skin smooth, moist, and slippery.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Combining these pairs: Bile – Emulsification of dietary fats; Gastric juice and HCl – Breakdown of food to produce chyme in stomach; Pancreatic juice – Digestion of carbohydrates and proteins; Mucus – Keeps skin smooth, moist, and slippery. Thus, the correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

answer.text: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q06 - Male reproductive structures of frog and their features

questiontext.text:
Match the structures of the male urinogenital system of frog in List I with their descriptions in List II:

List I List II
A. MesorchiumI. 10 to 12 fine ducts emerging from testes and entering kidneys
B. Vasa efferentiaII. Ducts carrying both urine and spermatozoa to cloaca
C. Bidder's canalIII. Double fold of peritoneum anchoring testes to upper kidneys
D. Male uretersIV. Longitudinal canal in kidney receiving vasa efferentia

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the role and structure of the mesorchium.
In male frogs, the pair of yellowish ovoid testes is suspended and adhered to the antero-dorsal surface of the kidneys by a specialized double fold of peritoneum called the mesorchium. Therefore, mesorchium matches with double fold of peritoneum anchoring testes to upper kidneys.

Step 2: Identify the origin and number of vasa efferentia.
There are 10 to 12 vasa efferentia that emerge from each testis, penetrate the medial border of the kidney, and communicate internally. Therefore, vasa efferentia matches with 10 to 12 fine ducts emerging from testes and entering kidneys.

Step 3: Trace the location of Bidder's canal.
Inside the kidney of a male frog, the vasa efferentia open directly into a longitudinal duct known as Bidder's canal, which then connects with the ureter. Therefore, Bidder's canal matches with longitudinal canal in kidney receiving vasa efferentia.

Step 4: Characterize the male ureters.
In male frogs, because the ureters convey both urine from the kidneys and spermatozoa from Bidder's canal into the cloaca, they function as urinogenital ducts. Therefore, male ureters match with ducts carrying both urine and spermatozoa to cloaca.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Combining these pairs: Mesorchium – Double fold of peritoneum anchoring testes to upper kidneys; Vasa efferentia – 10 to 12 fine ducts emerging from testes and entering kidneys; Bidder's canal – Longitudinal canal in kidney receiving vasa efferentia; Male ureters – Ducts carrying both urine and spermatozoa to cloaca. Thus, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q07 - Physiological and ecological adaptations of Indian frog

questiontext.text:
Match the biological terms related to frog adaptations in List I with their descriptions in List II:

List I List II
A. PoikilothermyI. Body temperature fluctuates with ambient environmental temperature
B. CamouflageII. Summer sleep in deep burrows during peak hot periods
C. AestivationIII. Transformation of larval tadpole into an adult frog
D. MetamorphosisIV. Ability to change skin colour to blend into surroundings and evade predators

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Define poikilothermy in frogs.
Frogs are cold-blooded animals or poikilotherms because they lack intrinsic thermoregulation and their core body temperature fluctuates according to the temperature of the surrounding environment. Therefore, poikilothermy matches with body temperature fluctuates with ambient environmental temperature.

Step 2: Define camouflage in frogs.
Frogs exhibit camouflage (mimicry/protective coloration) by altering skin pigmentation to blend in with green grasses or dry terrain, concealing them from predators. Therefore, camouflage matches with ability to change skin colour to blend into surroundings and evade predators.

Step 3: Define aestivation in frogs.
During peak summer heat and drought, frogs take refuge deep in moist burrows to minimize thermal stress and desiccation, a dormancy period termed summer sleep or aestivation. Therefore, aestivation matches with summer sleep in deep burrows during peak hot periods.

Step 4: Define metamorphosis in frogs.
Development in frogs involves an indirect life cycle where the aquatic, tailed, gill-bearing tadpole undergoes drastic anatomical remodeling to produce the terrestrial adult frog. Therefore, metamorphosis matches with transformation of larval tadpole into an adult frog.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Pairing each concept: Poikilothermy – Body temperature fluctuates with ambient environmental temperature; Camouflage – Ability to change skin colour to blend into surroundings and evade predators; Aestivation – Summer sleep in deep burrows during peak hot periods; Metamorphosis – Transformation of larval tadpole into an adult frog. Thus, the correct matching is A-I, B-IV, C-II, D-III.

answer.text: A-I, B-IV, C-II, D-III
A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III
A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III
A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q08 - Body fluids and excretory structures in frog

questiontext.text:
Match the circulatory and excretory components of frog in List I with their defining characteristics in List II:

List I List II
A. Erythrocytes (RBCs)I. Structural and functional microscopic units of the kidney
B. LymphII. Circulating body fluid that lacks RBCs and a few blood proteins
C. Uriniferous tubulesIII. Thin-walled bilobed sac situated ventral to the rectum
D. Urinary bladderIV. Nucleated oval blood cells containing haemoglobin pigment

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze the erythrocytes of frog.
Unlike non-nucleated human red blood cells, the erythrocytes of frogs are biconvex, oval, nucleated, and contain the respiratory pigment haemoglobin. Therefore, erythrocytes (RBCs) match with nucleated oval blood cells containing haemoglobin pigment.

Step 2: Analyze the composition of lymph in frog.
The lymphatic system of frog contains lymph, lymph channels, and lymph nodes. Lymph is distinct from blood because it completely lacks erythrocytes (RBCs) and has lower concentrations of specific plasma proteins. Therefore, lymph matches with circulating body fluid that lacks RBCs and a few blood proteins.

Step 3: Analyze the functional units of the frog kidney.
Each dark-red, bean-like kidney is composed of thousands of structural and functional excretory units termed uriniferous tubules or nephrons. Therefore, uriniferous tubules match with structural and functional microscopic units of the kidney.

Step 4: Analyze the urinary bladder of frog.
In frogs, the urinary bladder is a thin-walled, distensible sac positioned ventrally with respect to the rectum that discharges its contents directly into the cloaca. Therefore, urinary bladder matches with thin-walled bilobed sac situated ventral to the rectum.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Synthesizing the matches: Erythrocytes (RBCs) – Nucleated oval blood cells containing haemoglobin pigment; Lymph – Circulating body fluid that lacks RBCs and a few blood proteins; Uriniferous tubules – Structural and functional microscopic units of the kidney; Urinary bladder – Thin-walled bilobed sac situated ventral to the rectum. Thus, the correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III.

answer.text: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q09 - Urinogenital structures in male and female frogs

questiontext.text:
Match the urinogenital organs of frog in List I with their anatomical connections or routes in List II:

List I List II
A. Female uretersI. Emerge from kidneys to carry both urine and spermatozoa into the cloaca
B. Male uretersII. Small median chamber receiving excretory, digestive, and genital outputs
C. Female ovariesIII. Transport only urine and open into the cloaca independently of oviducts
D. CloacaIV. Situated near the kidneys without any functional connection with them

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the female ureters.
In female frogs, the ureters conduct only urine from the kidneys and empty directly into the cloaca without merging with the genital system; the oviducts open into the cloaca through separate apertures. Therefore, female ureters match with transport only urine and open into the cloaca independently of oviducts.

Step 2: Evaluate the male ureters.
In male frogs, the ureters receive spermatozoa from Bidder's canal inside the kidneys and carry both urinary waste and gametes to the cloaca, thus functioning as urinogenital ducts. Therefore, male ureters match with emerge from kidneys to carry both urine and spermatozoa into the cloaca.

Step 3: Evaluate the anatomical relationship of female ovaries.
The pair of lobulated ovaries in female frogs is situated near the kidneys, but unlike the male testes, there is no structural or functional duct connection between the ovaries and the kidneys. Therefore, female ovaries match with situated near the kidneys without any functional connection with them.

Step 4: Evaluate the role of the cloaca.
The cloaca is a small, common median terminal chamber that receives undigested faecal matter from the rectum, urine from the ureters/urinary bladder, and gametes from the reproductive tract before discharging them to the exterior via the cloacal aperture. Therefore, cloaca matches with small median chamber receiving excretory, digestive, and genital outputs.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Combining these pairs: Female ureters – Transport only urine and open into the cloaca independently of oviducts; Male ureters – Emerge from kidneys to carry both urine and spermatozoa into the cloaca; Female ovaries – Situated near the kidneys without any functional connection with them; Cloaca – Small median chamber receiving excretory, digestive, and genital outputs. Thus, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

answer.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q10 - Organisation of nervous system and sense organs

questiontext.text:
Match the neural and sensory divisions of frog in List I with their constituents in List II:

List I List II
A. Central nervous systemI. Sensory papillae, taste buds, and nasal epithelium
B. Peripheral nervous systemII. Ten pairs of cranial nerves and paired spinal nerves
C. Well-organised sense organsIII. Brain protected in cranium and spinal cord in vertebral column
D. Cellular aggregations around nerve endingsIV. Spherical eyes situated in orbits and internal ears

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the constituents of the central nervous system.
The central nervous system of frog consists of the brain, enclosed inside the bony brain box or cranium, and the spinal cord, enclosed within the vertebral column. Therefore, central nervous system matches with brain protected in cranium and spinal cord in vertebral column.

Step 2: Identify the constituents of the peripheral nervous system.
The peripheral nervous system connects the central axis to body parts and is composed of ten pairs of cranial nerves emerging from the brain along with pairs of spinal nerves originating from the spinal cord. Therefore, peripheral nervous system matches with ten pairs of cranial nerves and paired spinal nerves.

Step 3: Distinguish the well-organised sense organs of frog.
Among the five sensory modalities present in frog, the eyes (spherical simple eyes situated in skull orbits) and internal ears (responsible for hearing and equilibrium) are anatomically complex, well-organised organs. Therefore, well-organised sense organs matches with spherical eyes situated in orbits and internal ears.

Step 4: Distinguish the simpler sensory receptor aggregations.
Unlike eyes and ears, the organs of touch (sensory papillae), taste (taste buds), and smell (nasal epithelium) are non-encapsulated, simple cellular aggregations organized around terminal nerve endings. Therefore, cellular aggregations around nerve endings matches with sensory papillae, taste buds, and nasal epithelium.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Combining these pairs: Central nervous system – Brain protected in cranium and spinal cord in vertebral column; Peripheral nervous system – Ten pairs of cranial nerves and paired spinal nerves; Well-organised sense organs – Spherical eyes situated in orbits and internal ears; Cellular aggregations around nerve endings – Sensory papillae, taste buds, and nasal epithelium. Thus, the correct matching is A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I.

answer.text: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Sequence of sperm transport in male frog

questiontext.text: Select the correct sequence representing the pathway of spermatozoa transport in a male frog (Rana tigrina) from their site of origin to the exterior:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the site of sperm production.
Spermatozoa are produced in the male gonads, the paired testes, which are situated on the antero-dorsal side of the kidneys.

Step 2: Trace sperm conduction from testes into the kidney.
From each testis, 10 to 12 fine ductules called vasa efferentia emerge, cross the mesorchium, enter the kidney on its medial side, and empty into Bidder's canal.

Step 3: Trace conduction through the longitudinal kidney duct.
Bidder's canal is situated inside the kidney and communicates directly with the urinogenital duct (ureter).

Step 4: Trace passage to the exterior.
The urinogenital duct emerges from the kidney and leads into the cloaca, from which spermatozoa exit to the exterior through the cloacal aperture during amplexus.

Step 5: Final conceptual sequence.
The complete anatomical sequence of sperm transit in male frog is: Testes → Vasa efferentia → Bidder's canal → Urinogenital duct → Cloaca.

answer.text: Testes → Bidder's canal → Vasa efferentia → Urinogenital duct → Cloaca
Testes → Vasa efferentia → Bidder's canal → Urinogenital duct → Cloaca
Testes → Vasa efferentia → Urinogenital duct → Bidder's canal → Cloaca
Testes → Urinogenital duct → Vasa efferentia → Bidder's canal → Cloaca

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Sequence of food transit in alimentary canal

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following anatomical components of the alimentary canal of frog in the correct chronological sequence of food transit, beginning from ingestion to the expulsion of undigested waste:

  1. Duodenum
  2. Oesophagus
  3. Buccal cavity
  4. Cloaca
  5. Stomach
  6. Rectum

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify ingestion and initial passage.
Food is captured by the bilobed muscular tongue and enters through the mouth into the buccal cavity (III), which opens into the short tube-like oesophagus (II) via the pharynx.

Step 2: Trace gastric entry and processing.
The oesophagus conducts ingested food into the stomach (V), where chemical digestion by hydrochloric acid and gastric juices breaks food down into chyme.

Step 3: Trace intestinal transit and digestion.
Partially digested chyme passes from the stomach into the first segment of the small intestine, the duodenum (I), which receives bile and pancreatic juice via a common bile duct.

Step 4: Trace terminal transit and egestion.
Following final digestion and absorption in the intestine, undigested solid wastes move into the rectum (VI), which subsequently passes them into the common median chamber, the cloaca (IV), to be discharged through the cloacal aperture.

Step 5: Final conceptual sequence.
The correct linear sequence of food transit through the alimentary canal is: Buccal cavity (III) → Oesophagus (II) → Stomach (V) → Duodenum (I) → Rectum (VI) → Cloaca (IV).

answer.text: III → V → II → I → VI → IV
III → II → I → V → VI → IV
II → III → V → I → IV → VI
III → II → V → I → VI → IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q01 - Four basic tissue types in complex animals

questiontext.text: All complex multicellular animals are composed of how many basic types of tissues?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Fundamental Concept
In multicellular animals, cells are organized into tissues. A tissue is defined as a group of similar cells along with intercellular substances performing a specific function.

Step 2: Analysis of Animal Tissues
All complex animals, despite their structural diversity, are formed from only four basic types of tissues: epithelial tissue, connective tissue, muscular tissue, and neural tissue.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The human body and all other complex animals are formed of exactly four basic types of tissues.

answer.text: Four basic types of tissues
Two basic types of tissues
Six basic types of tissues
Eight basic types of tissues

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q02 - Zoological name of Indian bullfrog

questiontext.text: What is the scientific name of the most common species of frog found in India?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Taxonomic Classification
Frogs belong to the class Amphibia under the phylum Chordata and are adapted to live both in freshwater and on land.

Step 2: Identification of Common Species
The most prevalent and widely distributed species of frog inhabiting India is the Indian bullfrog, zoologically designated as Rana tigrina.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct zoological name of the common Indian frog is Rana tigrina.

answer.text: Bufo melanostictus
Rana tigrina

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q03 - Body regions absent in frog morphology

questiontext.text: The body of a frog is distinctly divisible into head and trunk. Which of the following anatomical regions are completely absent?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: External Morphological Divisions
The external body organization of an adult frog is streamlined for leaping and swimming.

Step 2: Evaluation of Body Regions
The body of an adult frog is divided into only two distinct regions: the head and the trunk. Intermediate connecting structures like the neck and a terminal appendage like the tail are completely absent in the adult.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The regions that are absent in an adult frog are the neck and the tail.

answer.text: Head and neck
Trunk and abdomen
Neck and tail
Thorax and tail

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q04 - Water intake mechanism in frogs

questiontext.text: How does a frog meet its water requirement from the environment?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Physiological Adaptation of Frog Skin
Frog skin is thin, highly vascularized, and kept permanently moist and slippery by secretions from mucous glands.

Step 2: Mechanism of Hydration
Frogs do not ingest liquid water through the oral opening. Instead, their permeable integument allows rapid osmotic absorption of moisture directly from the aquatic or damp terrestrial environment.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
A frog never drinks water orally; rather, it absorbs water directly through its moist skin.

answer.text: It drinks water directly through the mouth like terrestrial mammals
It absorbs water vapor primarily through the pulmonary epithelium
It takes in water solely through the cloacal aperture during swimming
It never drinks water but absorbs it directly through the skin

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q05 - Chamber composition of the frog heart

questiontext.text: How many chambers are present in the muscular heart of an adult frog?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Cardiac Anatomy in Amphibians
The heart of an adult amphibian is a muscular organ enclosed within a protective double-layered membrane called the pericardium.

Step 2: Identification of Chambers
The heart of the frog consists of three internal chambers: two thin-walled receiving chambers called atria (right and left atria) and a single thick-walled pumping chamber called the ventricle.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The frog heart has three chambers, comprising two atria and one single ventricle.

answer.text: Three chambers (two atria and one ventricle)
Two chambers (one atrium and one ventricle)
Four chambers (two atria and two ventricles)
Three chambers (one atrium and two ventricles)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q06 - Nitrogenous excretory product of adult frog

questiontext.text: What is the principal nitrogenous waste excreted by an adult frog, and what is the corresponding excretory category?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Nitrogenous Waste Elimination
The excretory system of the frog filters metabolic wastes from the blood through the functional units of the kidneys known as uriniferous tubules or nephrons.

Step 2: Chemical Nature of Excretion
The liver synthesizes urea from metabolic byproducts, and the kidneys excrete this dissolved compound into the urine. Animals that primarily eliminate urea are classified as ureotelic.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The adult frog primarily eliminates urea and is therefore classified as a ureotelic animal.

answer.text: Uric acid, making the frog uricotelic
Urea, making the frog ureotelic
Ammonia, making the frog ammonotelic
Guanine, making the frog guanotelic

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q07 - Number of cranial nerve pairs in frog

questiontext.text: How many pairs of cranial nerves originate from the brain of a frog?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Peripheral Nervous System Architecture
The peripheral nervous system of the frog comprises nerves branching directly from the central nervous system, including cranial nerves from the brain and spinal nerves from the spinal cord.

Step 2: Enumeration of Cranial Nerves
In amphibians like the frog, there are exactly 10 pairs of cranial nerves arising from various parts of the brain and passing through the cranium to innervate peripheral structures.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The frog possesses exactly 10 pairs of cranial nerves.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q08 - Protective eye membrane of frog

questiontext.text: Which transparent protective structure covers the bulged eyes of a frog while it remains submerged in water?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Ocular Adaptations in Amphibians
The eyes of the frog are spherical structures situated within orbit cavities of the skull, protruding prominently above the dorsal head surface.

Step 2: Subaquatic Protection
To protect the eyes from water-borne debris and mechanical irritation while allowing light perception under water, the eyes are covered by a transparent third eyelid known as the nictitating membrane.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The protective structure shielding the eyes while in water is the nictitating membrane.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q09 - Number of ova laid by female frog

questiontext.text: Approximately how many ova are released at a time by a mature female frog during oviposition?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Female Reproductive Capacity
A mature female frog possesses a pair of large lobulated ovaries situated near the kidneys that produce female gametes.

Step 2: Quantitative Gamete Output
During breeding, the female discharges a massive clutch of eggs into the water to ensure successful external fertilisation. A mature female lays between 2500 and 3000 ova at a time.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
A mature female frog lays 2500 to 3000 ova at a time.

answer.text: 50 to 100 ova

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q10 - Peritoneum fold suspending testes in male frog

questiontext.text: The yellowish ovoid testes in a male frog are kept attached to the upper part of the kidneys by which structure?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Anatomy of Male Gonads
In male frogs, the primary reproductive organs consist of a pair of compact, ovoid, yellowish testes positioned over the anterior surface of the kidneys.

Step 2: Peritoneal Anchorage
These testes are securely adhered to the upper portion of the respective kidneys by a specialized double fold of the peritoneal membrane termed the mesorchium.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The testes are attached to the kidneys by a double fold of peritoneum called the mesorchium.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q11 - Tissue composition of vertebrate heart

questiontext.text: Which basic tissue types are present in the anatomical structure of the heart in complex animals?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Organ Level Organisation
Organs are formed by the cooperative association of tissues arranged in specific proportions and architectural patterns to perform specialized physiological roles.

Step 2: Tissue Distribution in the Heart
The heart exemplifies complex organ structure: its inner and outer surfaces are lined by epithelial tissue (endocardium and epicardium), its bulk pumping wall consists of muscular tissue (myocardium), its valves, fibrous skeleton, and blood vessels are supported by connective tissue, and its intrinsic conduction and regulation are provided by neural tissue.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The heart is constructed from all four basic animal tissues: epithelial, connective, muscular, and neural tissues.

answer.text: Muscular and neural tissues only
Muscular and connective tissues only
All four basic types: epithelial, connective, muscular, and neural tissues

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q12 - Dorsal and ventral skin colouration in frog

questiontext.text: Which combination correctly describes the pigmentation and pattern of the dorsal and ventral body surfaces of Rana tigrina?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Countershading and Camouflage
The skin of the frog exhibits protective colouration (mimicry and camouflage) that conceals it from predators both from above and below.

Step 2: Detailed Pigmentation Analysis
The dorsal surface of the body is typically olive green mottled with dark irregular spots, matching vegetation and murky pond beds. Conversely, the ventral surface is uniformly pale yellow, blending with the bright water surface when viewed from beneath.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The dorsal side is olive green with dark irregular spots, whereas the ventral side is uniformly pale yellow.

answer.text: Uniformly pale yellow on the dorsal side and olive green with dark spots on the ventral side

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q13 - Structural differences between forelimbs and hindlimbs

questiontext.text: In Rana tigrina, how do the hindlimbs compare morphologically and anatomically to the forelimbs?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Locomotory Functions of Limbs
The limbs of the frog are adapted for dual habitats, assisting in swimming, walking, leaping, and burrowing.

Step 2: Comparative Digit and Size Analysis
The hindlimbs are considerably larger, stouter, and more muscular than the forelimbs to generate propulsive thrust during leaping. Anatomically, each hindlimb terminates in five digits connected by skin folds forming webbed feet. In contrast, each forelimb terminates in four non-webbed digits.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The hindlimbs are larger, more muscular, end in five digits, and possess webbed feet, whereas the forelimbs end in four digits.

answer.text: Hindlimbs are larger, more muscular, possess five digits, and feature webbed feet for swimming

Hindlimbs are equal in size to forelimbs and both end in five non-webbed digits

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q14 - Morphological markers of sexual dimorphism in male frogs

questiontext.text: Male frogs can be distinguished externally from female frogs during the breeding season by the presence of which combination of structures?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Concept of Sexual Dimorphism
Sexual dimorphism refers to distinct external phenotypic differences between males and females of the same species beyond their primary sex organs.

Step 2: Specific Male Secondary Sexual Characteristics
Male frogs uniquely possess sound-amplifying vocal sacs located at the throat angles that produce loud croaking calls to attract mates. Additionally, males develop an elevated, rough copulatory (nuptial) pad on the ventral surface of the first digit of each forelimb to grip the female during amplexus. Both structures are absent in female frogs.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Male frogs are distinguished by sound-producing vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of their forelimbs.

answer.text: Sound-producing vocal sacs and webbed digits on the hindlimbs only
Sound-producing vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimbs
